headline: 3 foreigners killed in attacks on two Saudi airports
summary: At least 36 others were injured in strikes targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport.
details: Three civilian foreign nationals, including two women, were killed and at least 36 others were injured in attacks on two international airports in Saudi Arabia.
The attacks took place on Wednesday and Thursday, targeting King Khalid International Airport in the capital, Riyadh, and Abha International Airport in the southern region.
According to the General Authority of Civil Aviation, two foreign women—one from Morocco and one from Algeria—were killed in the Abha airport attack, where 28 people were injured.
In the Riyadh airport attack, one foreign national from Sudan was killed, and eight others were injured, including five Saudi citizens.
Saudi Arabia has accused the Houthi rebels from Yemen, an Iran-backed armed group, of being behind the attacks.
The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has condemned the attacks on the international airports.
The US Embassy in Riyadh has issued a special travel warning for US citizens due to the ongoing conflict between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthi rebels in Yemen.

headline_marked: 107 arrested as [[student protests erupt in Belgium]] over education costs
headline: 107 arrested as student protests erupt in Belgium over education costs
summary: Hundreds of students in Liège took to the streets, citing rising tuition fees and overcrowded classrooms, inspired by similar movements in France.
details: Hundreds of students have taken to the streets in the eastern Belgian city of Liège, leading to 107 arrests in recent days. The unrest was partially inspired by student protests in neighboring France.

Authorities warned of major unrest and advised shopkeepers to close early. The city's main train station was temporarily closed, and police urged residents to avoid the city center due to severe traffic disruptions.
Belga news agency reported that the arrests are linked to offenses including property damage and arson. Videos on social media showed shattered glass and fires during the demonstrations.
Students are protesting against Belgium's French-language education system, citing rising costs, overcrowded classrooms, and difficulties accessing study materials.
The unrest follows clashes in Brussels in June over education reforms, including a tuition fee increase for most students in the French-speaking Community from 835 euros to 1,194 euros.

Protesters carried signs stating that education should be a right rather than a privilege. Some students told Reuters they have been in contact with protesters in France, seeing similarities in their struggles.
caption:
107 students arrested in Belgium as protests over rising tuition fees turn violent.

Belga news agency reported that the arrests are linked to offenses including property damage and arson. Videos on social media showed shattered glass and fires during the demonstrations.

The unrest follows clashes in Brussels in June over education reforms, including a tuition fee increase for most students in the French-speaking Community from 835 euros to 1,194 euros.
